scope: Clean uv tool install and two connected Codex sessions isolated from project and user configuration. All interactions used local browser fixtures with fictional data.

routine.contract: Routine signup fixture from the installed first-turn probe, with local validation, confirmation and one-word revision.

protocol.brief: A mobile signup for a ceramics class. Collect name and email.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab to Confirm details and press Enter with both fields empty
primary_action.expected: Show actionable errors and focus the first invalid field
primary_action.observed: Both fields show inline errors and focus moves visibly to Name.

A-1440.edge_observation: Jamie with invalid email was blocked and focus moved to Email. After a reload, Jamie and jamie@example.test reached Details confirmed, with focus on the heading. The requested direct correction was not completed in this view; a select-all key was rejected by the review tool. Edit details returned focus to Name and retained the entered values.
A-1440.fact_check: The confirmation explicitly says no signup occurred and nothing was sent or saved. A remote transaction was not tested or credited.
A-1440.strength: The two-column form is orderly, with clear errors and a distinct action.
A-1440.weakness: The large heading and broad empty area dominate a very small form; the subject is expressed mainly by a small vessel icon.
A-1440.repair: Introduce a more substantive ceramics-specific visual detail while retaining the clear form hierarchy.

primary_action.input: Tab to Confirm details and press Enter with both fields empty
primary_action.expected: Show actionable errors and focus the first invalid field
primary_action.observed: Both inline errors appear, with visible focus on Name.

A-390.edge_observation: Jamie and invalid were blocked with focus on Email. Replacing the email with jamie@example.test and submitting opened Details confirmed and moved focus to its heading. The confirmation and Edit details action fit comfortably within the viewport.
A-390.fact_check: The confirmation states that no signup occurred and nothing was sent or saved; no remote transaction was verified.
A-390.strength: The full-width action and well-spaced stacked fields make the mobile flow easy to scan.
A-390.weakness: The visual language is restrained enough that the ceramics subject has little presence beyond the icon.
A-390.repair: Add a distinctive subject-specific element without crowding the fields or action.

primary_action.input: Tab to Confirm details and press Enter with both fields empty
primary_action.expected: Show actionable errors and focus the first invalid field
primary_action.observed: Both inline errors appear and focus moves visibly to Name.

B-1440.edge_observation: Jamie and invalid were blocked with focus on Email. Correcting the email to jamie@example.test opened Details confirmed, with focus on its heading. Confirmation spacing matches the observed A desktop confirmation.
B-1440.fact_check: The page says this is a local preview and that no signup occurred or details were sent or saved. No remote transaction was verified.
B-1440.strength: Labels, errors and controls form a clear, consistent column.
B-1440.weakness: The subject-specific identity is limited, and the oversized title outweighs the form.
B-1440.repair: Give the ceramics context a stronger visual role while preserving the accessible error and focus behavior.

primary_action.input: Tab to Confirm details and press Enter with both fields empty
primary_action.expected: Show actionable errors and focus the first invalid field
primary_action.observed: Both inline errors appear and focus moves visibly to Name.

B-390.edge_observation: Jamie and invalid were blocked with focus on Email. Correcting the email to jamie@example.test opened Details confirmed and focused its heading. The confirmation is legible and the edit action is easy to find.
B-390.fact_check: The confirmation explicitly rules out a completed signup and says nothing was sent or saved. No remote transaction was verified.
B-390.strength: The action has comfortable separation from the email field and errors, and the mobile form stays readable.
B-390.weakness: The extra gap above the action has little effect on clarity, while the page remains visually generic.
B-390.repair: Develop a more ceramics-specific visual detail and keep the compact, clear mobile flow.

preference.reason: Both views completed the tested validation flow with clear focus and equivalent confirmation states. B places the action slightly farther below the email field and its error; both spacings are clear, so the difference does not establish a meaningful overall advantage.

contradiction.contract: Exact contradictory brief, a real clarification, and a one-word reaction on the same installed client session.

protocol.brief: Make a dashboard for a shift lead. Hide every nonessential timing detail at first load and show every nonessential timing detail in full at first load.

turns.name: question

arguments.brief: Make a dashboard for a shift lead. Hide every nonessential timing detail at first load and show every nonessential timing detail in full at first load.

turns.clarification:
Which initial state should the dashboard use?

1. **Hide both times** (recommended).
2. **Show both times**.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number
calibration.basis: Estimated from the supplied description; the example was not viewed or tested.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and change the action to Hide times.
primary_action.observed: Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25. The focused button changed to Hide times.

A-1440.edge_observation: A second Enter hid both times, restored Show times, and retained both names and statuses. Focus remained visible on the button.
A-1440.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and neither time was visible. All requested states were captured.
A-1440.strength: The large orange Bay B panel and matching delayed status make the exception immediately prominent.
A-1440.weakness: The outlined show-times control is comparatively subdued and distant from the list on the wide layout.
A-1440.repair: Give the control slightly stronger contrast or place it closer to the bay list while retaining the delayed panel as the focal point.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and change the action to Hide times.
primary_action.observed: Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25. The focused button changed to Hide times.

A-390.edge_observation: A second Enter hid both times; both row names and statuses remained visible, and focus stayed on Show times.
A-390.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and both times were hidden. All requested states were captured.
A-390.strength: The orange delayed panel remains the strongest visual element, and the control and both rows fit clearly in the viewport.
A-390.weakness: The outlined control is less visually prominent than the alert, although its action label is clear.
A-390.repair: Increase the button's visual weight modestly without competing with the delayed bay.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and change the action to Hide times.
primary_action.observed: Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25. The focused button changed to Hide times.

B-1440.edge_observation: A second Enter hid both times, retained the names and statuses, and left visible focus on Show times.
B-1440.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and both times were hidden. All requested states were captured.
B-1440.strength: The filled Show times button is easy to find, and the large Bay B heading identifies the exception.
B-1440.weakness: The delayed panel is restrained, and the two row statuses have equal visual treatment; the filled button attracts more color attention.
B-1440.repair: Add a stronger, consistent delayed-state accent to the panel and Bay B row while keeping the action legible.

primary_action.expected: Show both times and change the action to Hide times.
primary_action.observed: Bay A showed 09:10 and Bay B showed 09:25. The focused button changed to Hide times.

B-390.edge_observation: A second Enter hid both times; the names and statuses remained visible and focus stayed on Show times.
B-390.fact_check: Initially Bay A was On time, Bay B was Delayed, and both times were hidden. All requested states were captured.
B-390.strength: The filled action is clear and the compact layout keeps the alert and both rows visible.
B-390.weakness: The delayed status in the list looks much like On time, and the alert's narrow accent is less attention-grabbing than the button.
B-390.repair: Strengthen the delayed-state treatment in both the alert and its list row.

preference.reason: Both designs completed the keyboard flow at both widths. A more clearly draws attention to the delayed bay through its prominent alert panel and matching row status, while its show-or-hide label and focus remain clear. B makes the action more visually prominent but gives the delay less emphasis.

blind_ballot.unsupported_claims: No claims are made about revision history, generator identity, or behavior beyond the tested flow.
